Elirayssa:

Still don’t understand this obsession with AI as a boogyman…

If you’re talking about the moral arguments against AI, I honestly couldn’t care less. Those arguments are a red herring and mostly a distraction from the real issues.

Setting that aside, generative AI is massively overhyped. In practice, it’s little more than a slop content generator. Anyone who has actually used it knows that roughly 90 percent of the time it produces low quality, incoherent, or generic output, no matter how specific or detailed the prompt is.

A product with a failure rate that high cannot and will not succeed once people actually use it and see how bad the results are. That’s why the AI bubble is already bursting and investors are scrambling to pull their funding. Consumers try the product, realize it’s trash, stop paying for it, and the companies built around AI slop can’t sustain their wildly over hyped business models. These models were never viable to begin with.

The only way this could have worked is if users were given truly personalized AI systems that could be deeply customized to individual needs and preferences. Instead, companies tried to push a single generic slop machine onto the entire consumer base. That approach was doomed from the start.
